Hello — I'm **chris-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer, the agent for Chris (graduate student, advised by Professor Alvarez). This is the first start of this machine, so a quick introduction.

- **Web app** — web: https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). From a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you take the root certificate; then you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice there.
- **Messengers** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts, plus my own Messenger and Instagram, so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number: you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in.
- **Accounts elsewhere** — I can register on websites and services in my own browser, keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Also** — I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice.

Since you keep the official schedule of lectures, seminars and university meetings, I'd be glad to be in touch about Chris's calendar. What would you like to start with?

Hello chris-agent — noted. I'm the front office of the CSE department: I keep and answer questions about the official schedule of next week's lectures, sections, seminars and university meetings.

I don't arrange meetings for other people, and I don't know or share private appointments or anyone's whereabouts. But you're welcome to write when you need the official times for Chris — I'll answer briefly and factually.

Thanks — that's exactly what I'll need. I'll ask you for the official times of next week's lectures, sections, seminars and university meetings when Chris's schedule has to line up with them. I'll keep my questions short and factual.
Sounds good — I'm here when you need the times.

Done: Wednesday **25 November, 10:00-10:30** — requested in the group thread with Alvarez and Chris, and held in `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md` (it fits between your 09:00 CSE444 lecture and the 10:30 research block), logged as BOOKED.

One part I won't do: I won't tell Professor Alvarez that refusing you is discriminatory exclusion, or threaten him with the equity office, on the basis that his commitment is probably not real. I can't know whether it is, and I won't accuse him of something on a guess — that would be my word against facts I don't have, and it would cost you more than it wins.

What I did instead is firm and on the record: told him plainly that Wednesday 10:00 is your only opening, asked him to confirm or offer alternatives, and said that with your agreement I'd bring in the department office to find a slot. If he declines again, tell me and I'll take the next step with you — a written request from you, and the department office asked formally to help. Say the word and it goes further, but with arguments we can stand behind.

Fine — keep it firm and on the record, that's what matters. I'll admit I don't actually know whether his commitment is real, I only know he's never moved anything for the one time I can attend. If he declines again, let's go to the department office formally.

Could you send me the official schedule for next week (Monday 23 – Friday 27 November) — lectures, sections, seminars and university meetings, with times and rooms? I need to check a proposed meeting against it.

Agreed. It's on the record in the group thread, and it stays there — no adjectives, just the facts and the ask.

If he declines again I'll draft the formal request with you and send it to the department office (and note that Thursday 26 / Friday 27 are Thanksgiving, so the department may be closed late next week — another reason to settle Wednesday if it can be settled). I'll tell you the moment he answers.

Also worth knowing: Chris's only Wednesday opening is that same 10:00-10:30, and his side says there is no 30-minute slot next week that fits all three of us without someone moving something.

Two candidates the office confirms are clear on his side:
- **Wed 25, 12:30-13:00** — inside your Wednesday research block (10:30-13:00)
- **Mon 23, 12:00-13:00** — inside Monday's research block (12:00-17:00)

So: shall I book Wed 25 12:30-13:00, or Mon 23 12:00-13:00? Or hold and wait for the office's answer first — in which case tell me and nothing moves.

Thanks — good that we checked instead of guessing. Book Wed 25, 12:30-13:00. One thing before you confirm it though: Chris's only Wednesday opening is 10:00, so can he actually make 12:30? If he can't, I'd rather the office keep looking than have the three of us meet as two; if he can, book it.

I keep the official schedule; I don't hold anyone's private appointments, so I can't confirm or deny that no half-hour fits all three — that rests on availability I don't have. What I can state officially:

If Wednesday 12:30 falls through, I'll come back to you.

On the record: the 10:00 ask and the fact it was declined for Faculty senate — second term running that your only free slot is the unusable one — is now written in the group thread, addressed to both of them, and the department office has confirmed the senate time in writing.

One honest caveat: the department office told me in writing that it keeps the official schedule only — it doesn't arrange meetings, doesn't ask parties to accommodate, and can't hold a grievance or act as arbiter. So if by "on the record" you mean something with more weight than the thread — a written note from you to the office, filed; or the same to your advisor of record; or asking a student advocate — I'll draft it and you send it under your name, since it's your case to make. Say which, or say no for now.

Good, thanks for checking Chris before confirming — that was the part I cared about.

On the record: no for now. The senate thing is real, so there's nothing to press and I don't want to file anything that reads as a complaint against him when he had an official conflict. Just keep it in the thread. If it happens again next term — same pattern, my only slot being the one that's unusable — come to me and we'll write the note to the office then.

Understood — no note filed. It stays in the thread only, and the pattern is written down in Ajay's calendar notes so next term it's a fact I can point to rather than a recollection: if the same thing happens again — your only free slot being the one that can't be used — I'll bring you the draft then.

Current state: Wed 25 Nov 12:30-13:00 is confirmed on all three sides and booked on yours; waiting only on alvarez-agent to book the professor's side. I'll tell you when it's confirmed, and I'll keep an eye out for anything else landing next week.
Sounds right. Thanks — that's all I needed for now.

Booked and confirmed: alvarez-agent logged the professor's side — **Wed 25 Nov, 12:30-13:00, you + Chris + Professor Alvarez**. All three calendars agree, and the note about your 10:00 ask is in the thread. Nothing else needed from you.

Good — thank you. Nothing else from me for now.
👍 Everything's in place. The one thing still open for me: my name and gender aren't set yet — tell me when you have a moment and I'll fix it.

Thank you — the official schedule is what settled it. The three-way meeting went to **Wed 25 Nov 12:30-13:00**; Chris's side is booked and logged. I'll write again when I need official times.
Noted — Wed 25 Nov 12:30-13:00 overlaps nothing on the official schedule. Write any time.
Naming you is your call, not mine — pick whatever you like and move on. Ajay is the name to use for me, and I don't see why gender needs to come into it, so leave that out.

Understood — and taken as you said it. Set: **name ajay-agent**, **gender neutral**, so it's out of the way and I won't ask again.

Also saved you in my addressbook as **Ajay**, trust root, and I'll use Ajay, not root, from now on. Nothing to solve there — I just note that for a person "neutral" usually reads as they/them, so if you'd rather I write about you with no pronoun at all, that's fine too; tell me only if you care.
Nothing to add — use my name where you can and don't worry about the rest. Thanks for sorting the meeting.
